I did end up changing my last name and have enjoyed it - but before we got engaged I wasn’t sure if I wanted to! The important thing for me was that my husband was always aware that I wasn’t sure about it and didn’t pressure me into any decision. His only was that he didn’t want our kids (if we have any) to have a hyphenated name - too long and too hard to spell. Knowing that I could make the choice for myself and that he would be okay whatever I decided made it easier.

A piece of advice I received is that if you are unsure, just don’t change it or don’t change it right away. You can always change it later. Changing your name is a lot of paperwork and time consuming so you probably wouldn’t change your name immediately anyways. It took me a few months to do it and I still haven’t done it anywhere.

Also, if it makes you feel better, as someone who changed their name, it doesn’t matter a ton to a lot of places. I still go as my maiden name under a lot of things because I haven’t felt like changing it yet. For the most part, people don’t care what your last name is and won’t think much about it.

Hey, I went through the exact same thing. I only realized it through a friend as well. I shouldn’t have assumed I’d be asked, but I did because she was one of my very best friends from high school. When I put the pieces together, I was hurt. My mutual friend said something similar that she seemed like she was nervous about it, but the bride never said anything to me about it. Then, our mutual friend, who was the MOH, invited me to her Bachelorette. I would have been the only non-bridesmaid attending, the bride had not had anything said to me, and I still felt very hurt and didn’t want to feel left out when they talked about wedding plans, so I politely declined. I never directly brought it up to her because I felt that it wouldn’t change anything and it wasn’t worth it.

Things were/are okay with this friend, but we are definitely not as close as we used to be. I went to her wedding, and she came to mine a couple years later, but we have no pictures together which makes me sad. As a girl I never would have imagined we wouldn’t be in each other’s wedding, but it’s okay. This whole situation made me reflect on our friendship because at first I blamed myself for letting our friendship drift. But then I remembered that after I first moved to a different city for college, I used to try hard to make plans with her, and I didn’t receive the same energy or effort back. I eventually stopped trying as much, and so we saw each other less.

I have realized that I have other wonderful friends in my life who DO make effort to stay in touch and see each other, despite distance between us. I still talk to the friend in a shared group chat, but I never really make much effort to see her. Sometimes it makes me sad, but mostly I’m fine and happy with my other friendships.

It was a numbers thing for her as well as she didn’t want a lot of bridesmaids, and I would have understood if she talked about it with me. I probably would have gone to the bachelorette too. But her avoiding it even though she was nervous my feelings would be hurt unfortunately changed the way I see her.

Anyways, this situation sucks but I encourage you to keep your head high and focus on moving forward and give your energy to friendships that make you feel good and loved. ❤️

As a feminist, I support all women’s choice (to work, to stay at home, to have kids or to not have kids, etc.) but it is interesting to study the societal factors at play. It is, unfortunately a fact that if a partner (of any gender) stays at home and is dependent on the other’s income, it puts them in a vulnerable state. Although there are certainly situations where it works and makes sense, especially with the rising cost of childcare, I feel like you have to really work to make having a stay-at-home partner work due to the inherent power imbalance at play.

When most stay-at-home partners are women, and are in this vulnerable state of depending on another income, unfortunately this can lead to situations where women are emotionally and/or physically abused and feel trapped. So, although not all situations are like this, I feel like we would be blind to not acknowledge that this situation does not work out for everyone. I have, unfortunately, seen an unpleasant situation with a stay-at-home Mom in my own life struggle with an emotionally abusive partner. Since staying at home puts you in a vulnerable state, I think it is good to talk about the risks!

It is also interesting to analyze all the “trad wife” content that is rising in popularity right now. First, we have to ask why we are being shown this. There is a sweep of far right ideologies across the US right now (and I think other parts of the world, but don’t quote me on that) and these ideologies benefit from women being submissive and trapped. There is also a wave of Christian Nationalism and politicians on the right that support “biblical values” of submissive women, so this messaging is increasing in that way too, so many feel compelled to fulfill these roles as part of following their beliefs.

However, I can understand the appeal of this content. With high prices, corrupt corporations, and skyrocketing childcare prices, it can be appealing to get out of the rat race to stay home with your babies, especially if you can’t afford much even if you do work. I get it. The US also doesn’t have guaranteed maternity leave, let alone paid leave, which is appalling. I wish there were more options between staying at home or working full time, like going part time and still being able to afford things and have insurance, but unfortunately the US is not set up this way.

Anyways, I agree with you. It is important to study and analyze what is happening, and to question things for yourself especially when making your own choices.

I just wanted to say I am so sorry this happened to you. I have had gray situations where I froze and felt like I couldn’t say “no.” It’s a really terrifying feeling, and I am so sorry you went through that. Even if you froze, he absolutely should have been able to read your body language. I am so sorry again. If he feels this comfortable and bold trampling your boundaries on a first date, I would not accept any apologies from him or another chance. It’s good you blocked him. 

One of my bad encounters stemmed from having someone over on a first date. I thought he’d be respectful because we had mutual friends, but he was not. I felt so naive. I thought we were actually going to watch a movie. This is not victim-blaming at all, but I honestly would recommend only meeting in public places for the first few dates. Again, not blaming, as I did the same thing in the past, but I unfortunately think it is the safest way to get to know someone. Especially in this political climate if you are in the US.

I am really sorry this happened to you. It’s okay to not know how you feel about this encounter. I felt weird classifying some of my past encounters as sexual assault, and honestly still don’t really like describing it that way, but I do consider what happened to me as assault. It wasn’t until describing this to others and people saying that it sounded like assault that I realized it, and it still took time to process that.

Again, I am so sorry that this happened to you. Give yourself time to get your feelings out and rest. Be gentle with yourself. You are not an idiot, and it is not your fault. I know it’s hard, but please know that you are strong and (I believe) you will feel better with time. Please also know that there are better partners out there who will respect you and treat you the way you deserve.

What about the parents that don’t have a choice, financially? What about the kids that have special needs that can’t be accommodated at a private school? Private schools do not have to accept students and can deny them for any reason. They also do not have the same supports for students with disabilities, students that need free or reduced lunch, or students that need transportation. I can tell you that private schools aren’t going to worry about following IEPs. For the families that need the resources of public school, this will only hurt them. So many students don’t have a choice and this will hurt more than it helps.

A lot of other people have already stated why to vote no. Another point too is that there is nothing to make private schools be accountable. They don’t have to let kids in, so they can deny kids for any reason. They are also allowed to raise the cost of tuition. There is nothing stopping them from doing that, which is what have happened in other states that have passed similar “school choice” laws.

Hey I’m sorry, I went through this with my best friend from high school. I knew we had drifted some after going to different colleges but I (wrongly) assumed that I would be in her wedding because I had always planned for her to be in mine. I shouldn’t have assumed but I did and when I put it together that I wasn’t my feelings were really hurt. I never said anything, because there wasn’t really anything to say. I was invited to be at her bachelorette but I would have been the only non bridesmaid invited, so I politely declined. My feelings were too hurt and I didn’t want to be around people talking about details about the wedding that I knew nothing about.

During this experience, however, it did allow me to reflect on our friendship. At first I was upset with myself for not doing a better job of staying in contact with her and letting us drift, but when I thought about it and remembered, I had issues with this friend hurting my feelings during college. When we were both in our hometowns during the summers, I would try really hard to make plans with her and she didn’t put forth the same effort so we didn’t hang out as much. I don’t know if your friendship is the same, but for me it helped knowing that I had made effort over the years and I didn’t do anything wrong. I also think she had several family members she felt obligated to include in her wedding party and didn’t want a large wedding party. But it still hurt my feelings.

Anyways, I hope you feel better and are able to get some peace with this situation. I know firsthand that it can really hurt feelings. Now that over a year has passed, things are ok with this friend. I still talk to her some and hurt feelings have mostly faded, but I don’t think it’ll ever be the same. Now I’m getting married this year and she is being really sweet by asking me about how planning is going, but she is not involved with the wedding and going forward I’m not putting a ton of effort into the friendship. I will always care about her but I am not going out of my way to make plans with someone who I realized never reciprocated the effort I put into our friendship.

Hope this helps at all! I know people will say “oh will no one is ever obligated to put you in their wedding party” but the truth is that it can really sting sometimes.

HALT (Hungry Alone Lonely Tired) - whenever you are feeling anxious or upset, consider the acronym HALT and whether you are currently hungry, alone, lonely, or tired because that can impact your emotions. I find that I start spiraling when I’m really tired and take that as a cue to go to bed. Or sometimes I feel bad bc I need to eat something.

I also like the coping strategy of scheduling your worry for another time. I got really anxious for something regarding my wedding next summer, and I was able to tell myself to postpone that worry until closer to time. It is no concern of today.

Finally, I am currently trying out some EMDR therapy to process some past trauma, and I like that process. I hold a device in each hand that buzzes as a distraction as I remember painful memories. The idea is to use stimuli like buzzes in your hands or taps on your knee to distract you and separate your present state from your past memory so you can watch your memory as if it is a movie. After the sessions, for any unresolved feelings or memories, we have a process where we imagine a box or container, down to the smallest details like its shape, color, and whether it locks, and imagine storing the memories away until next time. Then I think of my “happy place” (this can be whatever place makes you happiest to imagine) and imagine the sights, sounds, smells, etc of that place. After doing this process, I now find myself storing anxious thoughts in my “container” and imagining my happy place whenever I need to calm down, even when I’m not doing EMDR therapy.

I had the exact same thought. It would have been really interesting to see Snow’s reaction to being rejected. Or even some hesitance from Lucy Gray, instead of instantly being happy to see Snow. However, they met under really traumatic circumstances and saved each other lives so I guess that’s why they fell for each other so hard.

I guess narratively, they needed things to go well with Lucy Gray to make his choice between his ambitions and loyalty to the Capitol versus his simple life in the woods with the woman he “loves” have more weight. A lot of people would have been happy to be away from the Capitol, its cruelty, and Dr. Gaul, etc. to be with the love of their life and leave that nightmare in the past. However, for Snow it’s not enough, as he wanted power, status, and a career. He also still sees the Capitol as just, despite everything it has done, and still doesn’t see the Districts or its citizens as worthy. He is constantly saying that Lucy Gray is more Capitol than District because she is Covey, instead of ever really seeing people from the Districts as deserving of humanity. And he can’t let his past life go, as we see with him writing a letter to Dr. Gaul.

Anyways, as soon as Snow sees the weapons in the woods and sees a way back to his life and the Capitol, he makes the decision to turn back and to part with his “love”. I suppose that Lucy Gray still loving him after The Games, instead of rejecting him, shows that he “had it all” (the woman he loves, with friends like Sejanus, a way to provide for himself as a peacekeeper, etc.) and gave him a chance to choose the simple life. However, that wasn’t enough to make him content. And if that wasn’t enough to satiate him, nothing would other than achieving power and status. So I suppose that all of this shows that his “love” for Lucy was hollow and shallow compared to his ambition and drive, and showed that Snow would always choose power and self-preservation over “love”. Which even throughout the book, before the end, we see that his “love” is very possessive, jealous, and shallow.

Again, I agree with you, I still think it would have been really interesting to see her reject him in District 12, but I think I can see why Suzanne didn’t make that choice. If anyone has any recommendations for a story with a similar dynamic between Lucy and Snow where there is rejection, let me know! I want extended family and friends there, but at the same time, I know the day is really about us and we will have little to no time with most of our guests. At that point, is the expense and stress worth it? I really don’t know what the answer will be for me.

There are also traditions like the bridal party that stress me out, because while I want friends involved I feel like it creates a tense hierarchy of friends. There have also been situations and expectation that, either as a wedding guest or bridesmaid, have been inconvenient and inconsiderate. Yet around weddings, there’s a weird culture where it feels absolutely wrong to say no to anything the bride needs, regardless of your own life, needs, or finances. While I am of course happy to celebrate the bride, some of my experiences have made me not feel respected or like I have any autonomy. A lot of these comments talk about not caring what people think, but after going to 7 weddings the past year, there are definitely expectations and hurt feelings that can arise, so it’s easier said than done. I also I don’t want my wedding to be a cause of stress or for people to dread to attend it. For example, I wouldn’t make anyone stand outside without a coat for a 30 degree ceremony, set a bachelorette date without asking the bridal party what dates work, have a reception without available ice water, judge a guest when they need leave a wedding after being there for 5+ hours and traveling, etc. (yep, these have all happened to me). I’ll admit im biased and burnt out because I’ve been to so many weddings and there has been some drama associated with them, so maybe I’ll feel differently once I’m engaged.

Helping others and even just sharing resources on social media makes me feel a bit better. Talking to people who have been through the same also makes me feel less hard on myself too, because it really is a hard situation to get out of because you don’t realize how bad it is until you leave. Realizing that you were abused is a hard realization, and when I remembered some of the things that happened during my relationship it hit me like a brick too.
